scholarships.title: Padua International Excellence Scholarship — Università degli Studi di Padova

existing.description: The University of Padua awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships each year to the most deserving international candidate on each degree programme delivered entirely in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional right-to-education tax and the revenue stamp payable. There is no separate scholarship application: applying to an eligible English-taught degree programme by its admission deadline makes the candidate eligible automatically. Selection is made by the Teaching Committee of each degree programme on academic excellence and the quality of the candidate's prior academic record, with the youngest candidate preferred in a tie.
eligibility: Does not hold Italian citizenship, unless the candidate holds dual citizenship
Holds a non-Italian secondary school diploma (bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes) or a foreign degree diploma (master's degree programmes)
Is not resident in Italy at the time of application
Applies for admission to an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua within the deadline set by that programme
Does not receive other scholarships or grants, which is a condition of receiving and keeping this award
Completes enrolment at the University of Padua
existing.eligibility_summary: Candidates must not hold Italian citizenship (dual citizenship is allowed), must hold a non-Italian secondary school diploma for bachelor's and single-cycle programmes or a foreign degree for master's programmes, must not be resident in Italy at the time of application, and must apply to an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua within that programme's deadline.
benefits: EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year, paid in two instalments of EUR 4,000.00
Exemption from student fees (contributi studenteschi) for each academic year of the award
coverage: EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year, paid in two instalments of EUR 4,000.00
Exemption from student fees (contributi studenteschi) for each academic year of the award
requirements: Apply for admission to an eligible English-taught degree programme by that programme's deadline; there is no separate scholarship application
Accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer, and pay the admission fee by the stated deadline
Meet the admission requirements, including obtaining the entry qualification, within the deadline in the admission offer
For non-EU candidates residing abroad, meet the requirements and conditions for an Italian student visa (D) for enrolment
Complete enrolment in the chosen degree programme, which is finalised after checks on the authenticity of the required documents
Hold an online bank account or prepaid card with an IBAN in an Italian or SEPA bank, in the student's own or joint name
Sign the Declaration of acceptance confirming the scholarship conditions and the absence of any incompatibility

Arrive in Padua by 15 December 2026 to receive the first instalment of the 2026/2027 award (30 November 2026 for awards funded by the Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering; this earlier date does not apply to awards from the Department of Industrial Engineering or the Department of Land, Environment, Agriculture and Forestry)
documents: Only the documents required to apply for the chosen degree programme; no additional documentation is needed for the scholarship
Online bank account or prepaid card with an IBAN at an Italian bank or any other bank in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), of which the student is the holder or joint holder
Signed Declaration of acceptance of the scholarship terms and confirmation of no incompatibility
For non-EU candidates residing abroad, an Italian student visa (D) for enrolment
existing.english_requirement: The degree programme must be taught completely in English. No separate English language test score is required by the scholarship itself; admission to the programme governs the language requirement.
application_method: Choose an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua and apply for admission within its application period
No separate scholarship application is needed; the degree application makes the candidate eligible for the competition
If shortlisted, receive a specific scholarship offer from the Admissions and Welcome Unit of the Global Engagement Office
Accept the admission and scholarship offers and pay the admission fee by the stated deadline
Complete enrolment and open or use an IBAN in an Italian or SEPA bank account
Sign and submit the Declaration of acceptance
existing.selection_notes: The Teaching Committee of each degree programme shortlists eligible applicants and awards the scholarship to the most deserving candidates on the basis of academic excellence in their field of study and the quality and results of their prior academic career. In case of equal scores the youngest candidate is given priority. Scholarships are mainly reserved for candidates applying in the first application period and may be awarded to second-period candidates only on an exceptional basis. Results are published on the University website on the dates set out in the Admission Notice.
existing.duration: 2 years for master's degree programmes; 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes
existing.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission call. For the 2026/2027 cycle the official call set first application periods of 2 November 2025 to 2 February 2026 for unlimited-access programmes and 7 January to 7 March 2026 for limited-access programmes, with scholarship results published from 11 March 2026 and 10 April 2026 respectively. The 2027/2028 call is due in November 2026.
existing.deadline_display: There is no separate scholarship deadline: the application for the degree programme automatically makes the candidate eligible, so the deadline is the admission deadline of the chosen degree programme, published in its Admission Notice. The call for the 2027/2028 edition had not yet been published on the verification date and the University states it will appear in November 2026.
existing.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in a completely English-taught degree programme: 2 years for master's degree programmes, 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes

scholarships.title: UniTrento Scholarships for International Students (non-EU candidates residing abroad)

existing.description: The University of Trento awards a limited number of merit scholarships to citizens of countries outside the European Union who live outside Italy and enrol in a degree programme, based on their admission score and programme of study. The scholarship is worth EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes, and scholarship holders are also exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on earning at least half of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions. The award lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the European Union
Living outside Italy at the time of application
Applying through the admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad for a University of Trento degree programme
Ranking high enough in the admission selection, since scholarships are limited in number and assigned on the admission score
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of a country outside the European Union who live outside Italy, applying to a degree programme at the University of Trento through the non-European admission call. Scholarships are limited in number and awarded on the basis of the admission score obtained in the selection.
benefits: Annual scholarship of EUR 7,200, or EUR 8,500 for female students enrolled in STEM programmes
Exemption from paying tuition fees for the year the scholarship is held
coverage: Annual scholarship of EUR 7,200, or EUR 8,500 for female students enrolled in STEM programmes
Exemption from paying tuition fees for the year the scholarship is held
requirements: Apply through the admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad for the specific degree programme; no separate scholarship application exists
Pay the EUR 30.00 application fee for the admission application
Earn at least 50% of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions to receive the second instalment on time
Alternatively, obtain 42 ECTS credits (36 on Italian-taught courses) by 10 August to have the second instalment paid in October
Hold an Italian or SEPA bank account or other arrangement required for the University to credit the instalments
documents: Admission application for the chosen degree programme through the non-European candidate call
Payment of the EUR 30.00 application fee
Academic curriculum and supporting documents required by the chosen degree programme's admission call
Documentation of non-EU citizenship and residence outside Italy
application_method: Apply for admission to the chosen degree programme through the annual call for non-European candidates residing abroad
Pay the application fee and submit the required academic documentation by that programme's deadline
Take part in the programme's selection, where the ranking score determines the admission and the scholarship award
Check the ranking list published by the programme, which shows both admitted candidates and scholarship assignation
Complete enrolment by the deadline communicated by UniTrento staff
Meet the credit milestones to keep the scholarship for the following year
existing.selection_notes: The selection is competitive: the University states scholarships are limited in number and based on the admission score obtained, and candidates do not need to apply separately for the scholarship. Ranking lists with admitted candidates and scholarship assignation are published by each degree programme. In September the University checks the credits earned by 10 August and confirms or does not confirm the scholarship for the following academic year; candidates who fall short must return part of the scholarship and pay tuition fees for the following year according to the published credit table.
existing.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme; up to 3 years for an undergraduate programme
existing.application_period: Tied to each degree programme's annual admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad. For the 2026/2027 cycle published deadlines included 4 March 2026 at 12:00 CET on several English-taught master's programmes and 23 March 2026 on others, each with a EUR 30.00 application fee.
existing.deadline_display: There is no separate scholarship call: scholarships are assigned through each degree programme's admission ranking, so the deadline is that programme's admission application deadline. The University of Trento's 2026/2027 admission calls for non-European candidates closed in March 2026, and the 2027/2028 calls had not been published on 4 October 2026.
existing.program_type: University merit scholarship awarded through the degree programme admission ranking, with a tuition-fee exemption; renewable on credit milestones
